body:
> Reported from the pipao-v2 board, where `hkb merge` has now done six merges under `merge.mode: "operator"`. It behaved correctly throughout — this is the one papercut, and it cost twenty minutes of looking in the wrong place.

## What happens

`hkb merge <n>` refuses a conflicted PR by passing GitHub's own message through: `Pull Request has merge conflicts`. Accurate, and useless when the operator then runs `git merge-tree` locally, sees a **clean** merge, and cannot reconcile the two answers.

The cause is that **GitHub does not run custom merge drivers**. A repo with

```
docs/wiki/log.md merge=union
```

in `.gitattributes` merges that file cleanly on any machine with the driver configured, and *conflicting* on GitHub's servers, which resolve with the built-in strategies only. Every worker PR appends to the wiki log, so once any one of them lands, every other open PR reads as `CONFLICTING` — and it compounds O(N²) across a merge queue.

This board has the same line in its own `.gitattributes`, so the same trap is loaded here; it has not fired yet only because the recent conflicts happened to be in source files.

## Why it belongs to `hkb merge` and not to the operator

Value 5: every error says what to do next. The current one says what GitHub said, which points at the diff. The actual next step is to look at `.gitattributes` — a place nobody looks when git has just told them the merge is clean.

## Done when

- On a refusal for conflicts, `hkb merge` distinguishes the two cases rather than relaying one message for both: when GitHub reports the PR unmergeable **and** a local three-way merge of the two commits is clean, the error names custom merge drivers as the likely cause and points at `.gitattributes`; when both agree it is conflicted, the message is unchanged.
- The local check is cheap and never blocks the answer: one `git merge-tree`, skipped without complaint when the base or head commit is not present locally (an Actions dispatcher has no full clone), in which case the message stays today's.
- The driver detection names the file: the hint says *which* path carries a `merge=` attribute, not just that some do, so the operator can see whether it is the file the PR touches.
- A test covers the three states — agreed-conflicted, GitHub-only-conflicted with a `merge=` attribute present, and GitHub-only-conflicted with none — through the fake gh double.
- The union-driver trap is stated once where an adopter meets it: a line in the wiki page that covers merging.
goal: A conflict refusal that git disagrees with names custom merge drivers and the .gitattributes path carrying one, with the agreed-conflict message unchanged and all three states tested
title: hkb merge relays GitHub's conflict message for a conflict git says is clean, because GitHub does not run custom merge drivers
